title: Separability of Subsets in Infinite Groups
summary: We study the separability of subsets of an infinite group. Given an infinite group $G$ and subsets $A,B\subset G$, we say that $A$ and $B$ are separated in $G$ if there exists an infinite symmetric subset $X\subset G$ with $e\in X$ and $XAX\cap B=\varnothing$. Question 17.102 of the Kourovka Notebook raises a natural cardinal question: if $A$ and $B$ are disjoint and $|A|,|B|<|G|$, must they be separated?
